active.title: Trunk-based gitflow model (no integration branch) as an option of the project gitflow block
active.description: Deferred by ADR 0037 (operator grill 2026-09-24): the constitution frontmatter gitflow block has fixed roles today (principal, integration, work) with free names. A trunk-based model would drop the integration role — work branches merge straight into principal — as an opt-in shape of the same block, read by the same pre-push gate. Pick only when an operator or consumer asks for it; until then the three-role model is the only one.
active.provenance: operator grill 2026-09-24 (onboarding foundation, Q1-Q11), ADR 0037 consequences: 'Trunk-based (no integration branch) is a backlog item.'

active.title: Server-side gitflow enforcement for consumer repos (CI guard / rulesets reading the constitution gitflow)
active.description: Deferred by ADR 0040 (operator grill 2026-09-24): consumer enforcement is local only — the pre-push gate reading the constitution gitflow block; dd-gitflow-default/CICD-AUTOMATION.md is a reference document and the workspace writes no CI workflow into a consumer repo. A later evolution would add server-side enforcement (a CI guard job and/or branch rulesets) derived from the same gitflow block. Operator: 'no momento não devemos ter nada referente a jobs de CI no github... depois evoluiremos isso' — not before the operator reopens it.
active.provenance: operator grill 2026-09-24 (onboarding foundation, Q10), ADR 0040 consequences: 'Server-side enforcement for consumers (CI guard, rulesets) enters through the backlog.'

active.title: Per-repo gitflow override for an associated repo whose principal branch differs from the main repo's
active.description: Deferred by ADR 0046 (operator grill round 3, 2026-09-25): the pre-push gate resolves the gitflow from the pushed repo's own specs/constitution.md, else the owning context's main-repo constitution, else the default with a warning. An associated repo carries no specs/, so it inherits the main repo's gitflow block {principal, integration, work}. When an associated repo's principal (or integration) branch has a different name than the main repo's, the inherited block names the wrong branches and its pushes are judged against them. A later evolution would let the gitflow block (or a per-repo entry beside it) name an override for one associated repo, read by the same resolution at push time. Not before the operator reopens it.
active.provenance: operator grill 2026-09-25 (onboarding foundation, round 3, Q5), ADR 0046 consequences: 'A per-repo override for an associated repo whose principal differs is backlog.'; grill handoff 2026-09-25T050500Z-main-thread-foundation-grill-r3: 'Backlog to add: per-repo gitflow override for associated repos.'

active.title: An unbound session with no native id and no DADAIA_SESSION_ID is refused under worktrees/<r>/ without a Stall
active.description: Declared gap of rc-5 (SPEC AC1.1 bullet 4, PLAN: ADR 0116 carries it to candidate 6): on a harness without a native session id (Kimi, Cursor, Devin, Copilot) an unbound session that never exported DADAIA_SESSION_ID is not refused under worktrees/<r>/<name>/, because refusing it would be a Stall (the harness process env is not the shell env). repos/<r>/ stays merge-only for every session (0105). Also: sessionStart-only harnesses (Cursor, Copilot) renew the bind heartbeat only at session start, so the bind lapses one day after the last start and they re-bind per session (fail-closed).
